note: Common checklists added to every plan by the 'when' conditions. Each item has an optional 'cat' (paperwork, firearm, gear, clothing, meat, safety, vehicle, plan) for grouping inside a list. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.

items.t: BC hunting licence for this licence year, FWID (Fish and Wildlife ID) number known
Photo ID on me
items.why: Show it with your FWID when an officer asks

items.t: Every species licence I hold this year, used and unused, on me
Ducks, geese, coots, snipe, mourning doves or pigeons: federal bird permit with stamp, paper or on my phone
PAL (Possession and Acquisition Licence) in my wallet whenever I carry a firearm
items.why: Tip: habit, not a hunting rule

items.t: Licences in a zip bag, same pocket every time
Season open today for this species, sex and class in my exact MU (Management Unit)
items.why: Read the MU row, not the region headline

items.t: My MU confirmed on the official MU map
In season regulation changes checked at gov.bc.ca/huntingregulations
Legal start and stop times for today written down
items.why: Big game and upland: 1 hour each side of sunrise and sunset. Migratory birds: half an hour

items.t: No Shooting Areas, closed areas, parks and ecological reserves checked on the synopsis map
Private, fenced, posted or cultivated land: written permission in my pocket
items.why: Consent is the law; writing proves it

items.t: Reserve land on the route: permission from the band office to hunt on or cross it
100 m ring around every occupied house, barn, school and playground marked on my map
Area closures and fire restrictions checked (BC Wildfire Service)
Deer, elk or moose in the Kootenay: CWD (Chronic Wasting Disease) zone rules checked
Weather checked
Trip plan left: who, vehicle and plate, where you park, route, return time, call 911 if not back by
Phone charged, offline maps downloaded, power bank packed
RAPP (Report All Poachers and Polluters) 1 877 952 7277 saved in my phone
Tourniquet in the same pocket every hunt
items.why: Know how: take a course with tourniquet practice (Tip)

items.t: First aid kit: gauze, pressure bandage, gloves
Headlamp plus spare batteries
Lighter, waterproof matches, fire starter
Whistle
Extra food and 1 L of water or more
Paper map and compass
items.why: Phone batteries die in the cold

items.t: Satellite messenger charged with a plan, or iPhone 14 or later with SOS via satellite
Emergency blanket or small tarp
Knife and spare blades
Game bags and 15 m of rope (big game)
Sunglasses, sunscreen
Extra layer, rain shell, toque, spare gloves
Blaze orange vest and toque
items.why: Not required in BC (90%). Strong safety Tip

items.t: No cotton next to skin
ACTS and PROVE every time I pick up, put down, hand over or receive a firearm
Ammo for this hunt only: the load I zeroed or patterned
Earth behind every shot. Sky is never a backstop
Legal to shoot flowchart run before every shot: licence, hours, season, ID, road, 100 m, land, backstop, clean shot
Rifle zeroed at 100 m with the exact load I hunt with
3 to 4 boxes of the SAME load bought
Zero confirmed again before the season
Range test done: 12 rounds, cold barrel, 20 cm circles, from the positions I hunt in. Result in the Journal
My tested maximum range known
Shooting sticks or the rest I carry
Rangefinder
Before the trigger: broadside or quartering away, one spot picked, range inside my max
Backstop solid, no animal behind; sitting or sticks, not offhand; breathe half out, squeeze, follow through
No full metal jacket bullets for hunting
Magazine out and chamber empty before the truck or ATV (all terrain vehicle)
items.why: A loaded magazine clipped in counts as loaded in BC

items.t: Single projectile ban zones checked, e.g. 400 m of listed highways
No rimfire on deer, moose, elk, bear, sheep or goat
items.why: Rimfire big game: bobcat, lynx, wolverine only

items.t: Firearm case and lock in the vehicle
Plug in: no more than 3 shells in magazine and chamber
items.why: Needed for all bird hunting; for migratory birds the plug must need the gun taken apart

items.t: Patterned on paper with my hunting load and choke
items.why: Ducks: 90 to 140 pellets in a 76 cm circle at your range (70%)

items.t: Right shells: ducks, geese, coots, snipe non toxic only, nothing else in my pockets
items.why: Lead is fine for grouse, quail, partridge, pheasant, turkey, doves, pigeons

items.t: Choke rated for steel if shooting steel
Choke wrench and spare tubes
At least one clay session this season
Ear and eye protection
Only birds above head height with open sky or ground beyond
Shot falls 150 to 250 m away: never toward a road, house, crew or vehicle
Deer with a shotgun: 20 gauge or larger with No. 1 Buck or larger, or slugs
Migratory birds: 10 gauge or smaller, no slugs, one shotgun unless others are cased or taken apart
Magazine empty and chamber empty before the vehicle
Legal for small game, grouse, ptarmigan and turkey only among birds
items.why: Not for quail, chukar, partridge, pheasant, ducks or deer

items.t: .22 zeroed at 40 m with the ammunition I hunt with
Subsonic 40 grain hollow points
Head or neck shots on sitting animals only: grouse inside 25 m, hares 25 to 50 m
Dirt backstop every shot. A .22 carries over 1 km and skips off ice and water
Single projectile ban zones apply to a .22 too
Magazine out, chamber empty before the vehicle
Right bow class for the animal: deer B, C or D; elk, moose, bear A, C or D; upland and small game B, C or D; migratory birds D
Pull meets the class minimum, e.g. class D 18 kg (40 lb) within my draw length
Big game: broadheads at least 2.2 cm (7/8 in) wide
Crossbow uncocked in or on any vehicle. Never shoot a bow from a vehicle
Bow only season? A crossbow counts as a bow
Bowhunter education course through the BC Archery Association
ICBC (Insurance Corporation of British Columbia) registration copy on the quad, plate displayed
Driver's licence and photo ID in my jacket
Proof of $200,000 liability insurance for Forest Service Roads
Not registered yet? Book an Autoplan broker this week
Closure map for my MU downloaded offline
Region 3: no ATV for hunting in MUs 3-28, 3-29, 3-30, 1 September to 10 December
Region 3 above 1,700 m: existing roads and trails only
Fire centre ORV (Off Road Vehicle) ban checked the night before
Private land: owner's consent to ride
Approved helmet, eye protection, gloves, boots over the ankle
items.why: Helmet is the law on Crown land

items.t: Lights on from half an hour after sunset to half an hour before sunrise
Spark arrestor fitted in wildfire conditions
Tow strap, small tool kit, tire plug kit and pump
Spare fuel if the loop is over half a tank
First aid kit, fire kit, headlamp, whistle, water, food, warm layer
Magazine out and chamber empty before I touch the quad
Get off and step away from the quad, then load
Never hunt from the seat or rack. Never herd wildlife with it
Leaving it in remote country: firearm out of sight with a trigger or cable lock
Deer on the rack: quartered, low, centred, ride slower than you want
Quad on the truck: ramp straps plus 4 ratchet straps, recheck after 10 minutes
No alcohol. Logging trucks own the road
PFD (personal flotation device) on and zipped, over all my layers
items.why: The law says carry one each; an inflatable must be worn in an open boat

items.t: Any motor: proof of competency on board, usually the PCOC (Pleasure Craft Operator Card)
Motors adding up to 7.5 kW (about 10 hp) or more: pleasure craft licence copy on board
Buoyant heaving line, at least 15 m (50 ft)
Reboarding device unless the climb in is 0.5 m or less
Watertight flashlight or 3 flares
Paddle or oars, or an anchor with 15 m of line
Bailer or hand bilge pump
Pealess whistle or horn
Navigation lights for before sunrise and after sunset
Magnetic compass unless I stay in sight of seamarks
Kayak or no motor: PFD, heaving line, reboarding device if needed, bailer, whistle, light in the dark
items.why: Sealed sit on top kayak with PFDs worn: whistle, plus a light in the dark

items.t: Capacity plate checked: people, gear, guns and game
items.why: VERIFY the numbers on your own boat

items.t: River flow and tide checked before launch
Trip plan lists the boat. Daylight only on big rivers
Guns unloaded while the motor pushes the boat; cased is the safe habit
Ducks and geese: shoot only when beached, anchored or tied off, not gliding
Other game: no hunting from a boat while a motor propels it
Never stand to shoot. Sit square, one shooter at a time, back to back
Weight low and centred. One person moves at a time
Fetch birds by paddle or drift with every gun unloaded. Never lean out over the side
Wader belt cinched
Dry bag: spare warm layer, lighter, phone
Capsized: expect the gasp, stay with the boat, climb on the hull, HELP position
Salt water: VHF radio or satellite messenger, anchor from the bow only, cold water course first
Route traced on the offline map; plan A and plan B chosen
Good wind and bad wind written for each spot
Turn back time set: 1 hour before sunset
Pack out plan: trips counted, light counted
Load at the start of the walk, 15 m off the road, facing away from people and the car
Unload before every fence, log or bank. Lay the gun through, muzzle away
Walk in cool: start a little cold so the base layer stays dry
Quiet outer layer: wool or fleece, no nylon swish
Wind checker (powder puffer or thread)
Red light headlamp for the walk in
Tape over any clinking metal on pack and sling
Unscented soap, no UV brightener
STOP if lost: Stop, Think, Observe, Plan
Hikers met: unloaded, muzzle down, greet first
Trip plan has the camp location and the return day
Campfire ban status checked on the BC Wildfire Service app
items.why: Rules change through the fall: VERIFY each trip

items.t: Recreation sites: no shooting within 100 m of a structure, camping area or trailhead; no game residue dumped there
Legal hours checked for each day of the trip
Pack like you will sleep out: shelter, extra layers, food and water for the extra days
Spare batteries and power bank for every night
Spare dry clothes and boots in a dry bag
Meat hung in shade, off the ground, with air around it
Hang meat high or take it home: coyotes and ravens find it by morning
Gut piles and meat away from camp, trails and campsites
items.why: A carcass is a wildlife attractant

items.t: Firearms unloaded and locked or out of sight in camp
Leave camp cleaner than you found it: pack out everything, fire dead, meat pole down
Partner has his own BC licence, species licences and bird permit. No sharing
Each hunter notches only his own licence. No party hunting in BC
Each hunter has his own bag limit. Do not pool birds
Record of Receipt if the partner carries my game without me
Before the walk: who covers left, who covers right, and the stop signal
Walk side by side, always in sight. Middle and behind are no shot zones
Lose sight of each other: muzzles up or down, no shooting, call out
Never swing through your partner. Stop the swing, gun up, safety on
Push or pinch drives: no shot arc agreed before the first step
In a blind: left and right agreed before first light. In a boat: one shooter at a time
Blaze orange on both of us
Only one shoots at a deer unless a backup plan was agreed
After a shot, both unload and walk up together. The shooter leads
PROVE out loud at the car, each watching the other
Each hunter can call for help alone: iPhone SOS or a satellite messenger
Partner's phone number and the land address written on paper too
Non hunting companion carries no firearm and walks behind or beside, never ahead
Read Grandpa's rules together before opening day
Four layers: base, mid, insulation, shell
Puffy insulation packed for sitting still
Insulated waterproof boots, about 400 g for cold sits
Spare merino or synthetic socks in a zip bag
Toque, neck gaiter, thin shooting gloves plus warm mitts
Spare dry layer in a dry bag
Power bank kept warm: phone batteries die in the cold
Winter tires or chains for the route
items.why: Many BC highways need them from 1 October (70%)

items.t: Shovel, tow strap, booster cables
Full fuel tank before leaving pavement
Snow line and temperature checked for tomorrow
Turn back 1 hour before sunset: days are short
Hypothermia: fumbles, mumbles, stumbles. Shivering that stops is an emergency
Do not sweat on the climb and then sit still wet
.22 skips off frozen ground and ice: dirt backstop
Hard cold: open and prop the carcass so it cools inside before the outside freezes
Bear spray on the hip belt or chest, not in the pack
Practise drawing the spray in under 2 seconds, safety clip on
Spray at the ground a few metres in front of the bear, then sweep up. Not into the wind. Range about 3 to 10 m: read the can
Defensive black bear attack: spray; if it makes contact, play dead
Predatory attack (stalks you, or at night): spray, stand big, fight back
Cougar: never run, look big, back away slowly, fight back if attacked
Fresh sign, carcass smell or ravens circling: back out, talk loudly, spray ready
Bear spray on your belt while field dressing
A gut pile draws bears: move meat away from it fast and watch your back
No gut piles near towns, trails or campsites
items.why: A carcass is a legal attractant

items.t: Dangerous bear or cougar: report to RAPP 1 877 952 7277
Every firearm unloaded: nothing in the chamber or an attached magazine
Leaving the truck: locked trunk or locked compartment, or out of sight in the locked vehicle
No hunting or shooting from a vehicle
Not on or across the road allowance of a numbered highway or 2 lane public road: 15 m each side of the middle
Walk 15 m off any road, then load
Never use a vehicle to herd or harass wildlife
Road and FSR (Forest Service Road) closures checked; DriveBC for the highway
FSRs: logging trucks have the right of way, drive on the right, call kilometres on posted radio channels
Gates left exactly as I found them
Never park a hot vehicle on dry grass
Spare tire, jack, lug wrench
Shovel and tow strap
Booster cables or a jump pack
Full fuel tank
Spare dry clothes and boots
Extra water and food
Coolers pre chilled, block ice or frozen jugs, rack for the cooler bottom
Tarp for the truck bed, extra game bags and rope
Firearm case and lock
Paper map of the area
Forecast: wind direction and speed for morning and evening
Temperature and any snow line for tomorrow
Plan A spot fits tomorrow's wind; plan B fits the other wind
Sunrise and sunset written down; legal start and stop worked out
In season regulation changes checked online
Road and fire restrictions checked for the route
Trip plan left, return time set
Phone and power bank charged, offline maps downloaded
Day pack packed. Say what each item is for
Full kit on and a 20 minute walk: fix what rubs or rustles
Licences, ID and permits in the zip bag by the door
Ammo for this hunt only, counted
Cooler pre chilled, ice ready
Alarm set so I am in place before legal light

lists.title: After the shot and the kill

items.t: Stay still. Watch where it goes. Listen
Pin and flag where I shot from and where it stood
Wait before following: at least 30 minutes for big game
Read blood and hair at the hit site; flag every spot and walk beside the line
Lost the trail: back to the last flag, circles, then lanes. Get help
Legal hours and the no light rule checked before continuing
The law: all reasonable effort to find, finish and retrieve it, and count it in my bag
Trail onto posted or fenced land, a closed park or a No Shooting Area: stop and get permission or call an officer
items.why: No Trespass Act exception for wounded game

items.t: Approach from behind, rifle ready; confirm it is dead
Big game: species licence notched right away, before I touch or move the animal
Photo of the notched licence beside the animal
Evidence of sex left naturally attached: deer, unskinned tail plus testicle or udder
Antler restricted season: antlers on the skull plate kept with the licence
Record of Receipt filled if anyone else transports it
Compulsory inspection, compulsory report or Mandatory Hunter Report deadline noted. Deer need neither inspection nor report
Gloves on, rifle unloaded and set aside
Evidence of sex planned before the first cut
No gut contents on meat, or washed and dried at once
Every edible portion taken: deer neck, ribs, all four quarters, loins; birds both breasts
Bear: gall bladder stays at the site, or the whole gut pile is disposed of within 48 hours
Guts out or meat off within the hour
Carcass hung or propped open, in shade, off the ground; skinned if above freezing
Game bags on. No plastic, no tarp on a warm carcass
Below 4 C as fast as possible; ice in the cavity or cooler; thermometer in the cooler
Meat dry, never sitting in meltwater; drain open
Birds: gutted, crop out, cooled apart; wing or head left on
Bear meat marked: cook to 71 C or more
Knife and hands washed
Giving away migratory birds: labelled with name, contact information, date, permit number and signature, or preserved
Unpreserved migratory birds count in my possession limit, home freezer too
Every edible portion bagged and packed out; licence travels with the meat
Kootenay CWD zone: head off with 8 cm of neck, to a freezer within a week, ear card filled, location submitted, meat held for the result, tools bleached
Butcher: shop phoned, notched licence or Record of Receipt with the meat, evidence of sex on until butchered, receipt with FWID, licence number, species, sex
Packages labelled with species, cut, weight and date; freezer list on the door
Mount? Decide before any cut. No throat or brisket cuts; cape frozen or salted within 24 to 48 hours
Journal entry written: date, MU, species, what worked
Week 1: find my FWID in WILD (Wildlife Information and Licensing Data)
Week 1: BC hunting licence bought online
Week 1: species licences bought IN PERSON
items.why: Online orders are mailed, about 14 business days

items.t: Week 1: federal bird permit bought online and saved on my phone, if hunting ducks or geese
Partner: his own licences and permits bought
Week 1: shotgun picked and bought; plug present
Week 1: steel shot for ducks; lead or steel for upland birds
Week 1: scope and rings mounted by the shop or with a torque wrench
Week 1: 3 to 4 boxes of the SAME rifle load
Week 1: ask the landowner where every house, barn and neighbour is
Week 2: bore sight, then zero the rifle at 100 m
Week 2: 3 shot groups from a rest until they are tight
Week 2: shoot from sitting and kneeling with shooting sticks
Week 2: pattern the shotgun on paper with the hunting load
Week 2: at least one clay target session
Week 2: clothing, boots and waders bought; boots broken in for a week
Week 2: day pack and car kit built
Week 2: offline maps downloaded; map scouting done (slopes, benches, water, roads)
Week 2: legal to shoot flowchart practised in Field Mode
I can say all 9 legal to shoot steps from memory
I know today's legal start and end for deer and for ducks
I know my MU and today's open seasons, and read my MU rows out loud
Rangefinded the house and the road from each stand
First aid course with tourniquet practice booked
PROVE drill at the car, out loud, until it is boring
Compass bearing walked to a landmark and back
Hunt week: in season changes, closures, fire and road restrictions checked
Hunt week: trip plan left; cooler and ice ready
Go slow. Watch more than you walk
Passing on a shot that is too far or too risky is a win
